title: I made a little atmospheric samurai duel game in less than ONE HOUR
author: FUNdationOne
selftext:
Holy macaroni...

I made this little atmospheric samurai duel game in less than ONE HOUR using GPT-Astra.

It started from absolute scratch and it created all the 3D models you see, including all the animations, all the light and particle effects, and also all the sounds, menus and game mechanics.

You can try it out here: [https://one-cut.tenshis.chatgpt.site/](https://one-cut.tenshis.chatgpt.site/)

But if everyone can make a game in minutes now, who is even going to play all of them? Hopefully it doesn't end with everyone creating their own games, movies and music and nobody enjoying anyone else's. We're moving toward a world of ultra-personalized entertainment. And as amazing as that sounds, there is a real risk ultra-personalization can turn into ultra-isolation.

Interesting and scary times ahead...

comments.author: HeadlessFrogMan
comments.body: Could you please tell us about your prompt and process? Are all of those 3D models purely something that Astra assembled on it's own with Blender MCP or something else?

replies.author: FUNdationOne
replies.body:
It's all made in code using three.js, it didn't use any tools or mcp at all. And it one-shot most of if, the rest was just refinements.

Using three.js was more or less the only technical requirement i gave it, everything else in the prompts was atmospheric and game mechanic descriptions. And even those were mostly very high level, like "atmospheric Japanese courtyard with cherry trees and stone lanterns, slowly falling Cherry blossoms, add moss and cherry blossoms on the ground, small Japanese gardens with a bridge, use O'ren ishii duel from Kill Bill as inspiration" etc. 

The most detailed part of the instructions were the fight mechanics, the difficulty progression, how opponents change over time. This is where most polish prompts went into after a bit of Playtesting.

One polish round went into getting the samurai to look acceptable, the first iteration looked almost like Minecraft characters.

The goal wasn't to make a perfect game, but to see what I could build in about an hour on my 20$ gpt account.
